description: Browser-first voice agent scaffold — MediaRecorder captures mic audio, POSTs to /api/stt for transcription, /api/llm for the response, /api/tts for speech synthesis, then plays the returned audio. Zero SDK lock-in: raw Web APIs in the browser, server-side wiring is pluggable.

defaults.headline: Push-to-talk voice agent
defaults.subheadline: Hold the button, speak, release. STT → LLM → TTS round-trip in the browser.

gotchas: getUserMedia requires HTTPS outside localhost. Any non-localhost deployment behind plain HTTP will fail with NotAllowedError — either ship behind TLS or use a tunneled HTTPS URL for dev.

MediaRecorder MIME support varies by browser: Safari prefers audio/mp4, Chrome/Firefox prefer audio/webm;codecs=opus. Always call MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported() before `new MediaRecorder(stream, {mimeType})` or the constructor throws on Safari.

Safari autoplay policies block new Audio().play() without a prior user gesture. Trigger playback from the button click handler, not from a fetch .then() callback that may resolve after the gesture context expires.
Holding the stream open between turns drains the mic LED and frightens users. Call track.stop() on each track when the recording ends; re-request via getUserMedia on the next press.

Blob size after 10s of 48kHz opus is ~80KB — safe to POST as raw body. Do NOT base64-encode into a JSON field (1.33× payload bloat + parser overhead). Use fetch with blob body and Content-Type from recorder.mimeType.
iOS Safari requires playsinline on <audio> playback in some contexts and silently suppresses volume control — verify on a real device, simulator behaves differently.
